speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start with the fever: how high has it gone, and when did you first notice it alongside the wrist pain and skin lesions?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Have you noticed any rash on your wrists or palms, or any swelling in your joints other than the knee? Also, have you recently been to a freshwater lake or had contact with ticks during your camping trip?

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, ESR, CRP.
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology photos of skin lesions.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Iron deficiency anemia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That diagnosis of iron deficiency anemia does not explain your fever, chills, or the specific violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on your wrists and hands. Given your recent camping trip in Minnesota and the self-resolving knee pain, could you describe if the skin lesions are itchy or burning, and have you noticed any petechiae elsewhere?

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, ESR, CRP, Blood Culture.
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology photos of skin lesions.
